reason: The cited evidence supports the general role of high configurational entropy in stabilizing solid solutions (E2, E3) and the importance of atomic size differences (E1), but provides no specific support for the key premises about diffusion kinetics, kinetic barriers from lattice distortion, or the interplay between diffusion and entropy in governing nanoparticle stability.
premises: High configurational entropy stabilizes single-phase solid solutions in equiatomic multimetal nanoparticles at high temperatures.
Lattice distortion from moderate atomic size differences creates kinetic barriers that suppress atomic diffusion.
Similar diffusion kinetics among constituent metals are required to maintain phase homogeneity.
Significant differences in diffusion rates or larger atomic size mismatches lead to phase segregation or intermetallic formation.
The interplay between entropy stabilization and diffusion kinetics governs stability under catalytic/thermoelectric conditions.
